name: Mammogram Screening Study
description: Breast cancer death outcomes for mammogram vs control over 30 years. IMS Ch. 17.
studyDescription: The Canadian National Breast Screening Study enrolled 89,835 women aged 40-59 and randomly assigned them to receive either annual mammogram screening (n = 44,925) or standard care without mammograms (n = 44,910). Researchers followed participants for 25 years and recorded breast cancer death outcomes. This is a large-scale randomized controlled trial.

variableDescriptions.group: Whether the woman was randomly assigned to the mammogram screening group or the control (no mammogram) group.
variableDescriptions.outcome: Whether the woman died of breast cancer during the follow-up period (yes) or not (no).

sourceDetail: OpenIntro IMS, Chapter 17. Based on Miller et al. (2014), 'Twenty five year follow-up for breast cancer incidence and mortality of the Canadian National Breast Screening Study,' BMJ.

context.nullClaim: mammogram screening has no effect on breast cancer death rate

inferenceContexts.parameter: the difference in breast cancer death rates between mammogram screening and control groups
inferenceContexts.claim: there is a difference in breast cancer death rates between women who received mammograms and those who did not
